title: I don't think so: aẓunn
goal: In a university corridor, guess with Sēf why the lecturer hasn't turned up
tip: aẓunn 'I think' goes straight before a sentence: aẓunn il-muḥāẓra bāchir 'I think the lecture's tomorrow'. For 'he', 'she', 'it' you usually add inn- + ending: aẓunn innah nisa 'I think he forgot', but you can drop it: ma aẓunn nisa. ma aẓunn alone: 'I don't think so'. Ask tẓunn? (woman: tẓunnīn?).
grammar: aẓunn + sentence 'I think'; ma aẓunn 'I don't think so'; tẓunn? 'do you think?'
dialogue: A
الدكتور للحين ما يا. تظن في محاضرة اليوم؟
id-daktōr lil-ḥīn ma yā. tẓunn fī muḥāẓra l-yōm?
The lecturer still hasn't come. Do you think there's a lecture today?
B
ما أظن. صار لنا نص ساعة نتريا
ma aẓunn. ṣār-lna nuṣṣ sāʿa nitrayya
I don't think so. We've been waiting for half an hour.
A
أظن إنه نسى. هو دوم ينسى!
aẓunn innah nisa. huwa dōm yinsa!
I think he forgot. He's always forgetting!
B
لا، ما أظن نسى. أظن إنه في الزحمة
la, ma aẓunn nisa. aẓunn innah fi z-zaḥma
No, I don't think he forgot. I think he's stuck in traffic.
A
شوف الإيميل! يقولون المحاضرة باكر
shūf il-īmēl! ygūlūn il-muḥāẓra bāchir
Look at the email! They say the lecture's tomorrow.
B
زين. تظن بيعطينا امتحان باكر؟
zēn. tẓunn biyaʿṭīna imtiḥān bāchir?
OK. Do you think he'll give us a test tomorrow?
A
هيه، على ما أظن. قال لنا الأسبوع اللي طاف
hē, ʿala ma aẓunn. gāl-lna l-usbūʿ illi ṭāf
Yes, I think so. He told us last week.
B
عيل خلنا ندرس اليوم في المكتبة
ʿayal khallna nidris il-yōm fi l-maktaba
Then let's study in the library today.
items: I don't think so; I don't think (that)
I think so, as far as I know
she forgot: nisat (نست); I forgot: nisēt
in the traffic, stuck in traffic
I forget: ansa (أنسى); dōm yinsa = he's always forgetting

title: In my opinion, the desert: b-raʼyi
goal: Plan the weekend with Sēf and Fahad, and give your opinion with a reason
tip: b-raʼyi 'in my opinion' starts the sentence: b-raʼyi l-barr aḥsan. More common and casual: ana ashūf 'I reckon'. To ask, say shu raʼyak? (to a woman: shu raʼyich?): b-rāyak alone means 'suit yourself'. Give the reason with lann before a noun: lann il-jaww ḥilu; with no noun, lannah: lannah garīb.
grammar: b-raʼyi / ana ashūf 'in my view'; lann / lannah 'because' to give a reason
dialogue: A
يا شباب، الويكند ياي. البر ولّا البحر؟
yā shabāb, il-wīkind yāy. il-barr walla l-baḥar?
Guys, the weekend's coming up. The desert or the beach?
B
برأيي البر، لأن الجو حلو هالأيام
b-raʼyi l-barr, lann il-jaww ḥilu hal-ayyām
In my opinion the desert, because the weather's nice at the moment.
A
إيه والله! وأنا أشوف البحر الحين بارد حيل
ēh wallāh! w ana ashūf il-baḥar il-ḥīn bārid ḥēl
Oh yes, definitely! And I reckon the sea's really cold now.
B
وانت يا سيف؟ شو رأيك؟ شو أحسن؟
w inta yā Sēf? shu raʼyak? shu aḥsan?
What about you, Sēf? What do you think? Which is better?
A
على كيفكم. بس البحر أحسن، لأنه قريب
ʿala kēfkum. bas il-baḥar aḥsan, lannah garīb
Up to you. But the beach is better, because it's close.
B
أظن البر مب بعيد بسيارة فهد!
aẓunn il-barr mub baʿīd b-sayyārat Fahad!
I think the desert's not far in Fahad's car!
A
خلاص، نروح بسيارتي. بس الأكل عليكم
khalāṣ, nrūḥ b-sayyārti. bas il-akil ʿalēkum
Fine, we'll go in my car. But the food's on you two.
B
اتفقنا! وأنا بييب الحطب
ittafagna! w ana bayīb il-ḥaṭab
Deal! And I'll bring the firewood.
items: you'll see written برايي; more common and casual: ana ashūf (أنا أشوف); on its own, b-rāyak (برايك) means 'suit yourself', not 'what do you think?'
I reckon, the way I see it
to ask: shu raʼyak? (to a man), shu raʼyich? (to a woman); b-rāyak (برايك) on its own means 'suit yourself, your call', not 'what do you think?'
ʿashān (عشان) works in the same place
up to you, as you like (to a group)
to one man: ʿala kēfak; to one woman: ʿala kēfich
in your car: b-sayyārtak (to a man), b-sayyārtich (to a woman)

title: The first time I've seen stars like that
goal: At Bū Rāshid's majlis, tell him what you've tried in the UAE and what you'd still like to try
tip: Talk about experiences with the past: jarrabt 'I've tried', rikabt 'I rode'. The question is the same form: jarrabt iṣ-ṣēd? 'have you tried fishing?' awwal marra + a present verb means 'the first time I've …': awwal marra ashūf nujūm chī. For 'not yet', say la, lil-ḥīn.
grammar: recycle: past tense for experiences; awwal marra + present verb
dialogue: A
يا ولدي، استانست في الإمارات هالسنة؟
yā wildi, istānast fi l-Imārāt has-sana?
Son, have you enjoyed yourself in the Emirates this year?
B
وايد يا عمي! كل شي هني تجربة يديدة
wāyid yā ʿammi! kill shay hni tajruba yidīda
Very much, uncle! Everything here is a new experience.
A
ما شاء الله. وشو أحلى شي جربته؟
mā shāʼ allāh. w shu aḥla shay jarrabtah?
That's wonderful. And what's the best thing you've tried?
B
نمت في البر وركبت بعير. أول مرة أشوف نجوم جي!
nimt fi l-barr w rikabt biʿīr. awwal marra ashūf nujūm chī!
I slept out in the desert and rode a camel. The first time I've seen stars like that!
A
صج؟ والبحر؟ جربت الصيد بالطراد؟
ṣij? w il-baḥar? jarrabt iṣ-ṣēd biṭ-ṭarrād?
Really? And the sea? Have you tried fishing from a boat?
B
لا، للحين. بس ودي أجربه
la, lil-ḥīn. bas widdi ajarrbah
No, not yet. But I'd love to try it.
A
عيل يوم السبت بنطلع بالطراد. لازم تيي ويانا
ʿayal yōm is-sabt biniṭlaʿ biṭ-ṭarrād. lāzim tiyi wiyyāna
Then on Saturday we'll go out in the boat. You must come with us.
B
إن شاء الله يا عمي، أكيد! هالسنة ما أنساها أبد!
in shāʼ allāh yā ʿammi, akīd! has-sana ma ansāha abad!
God willing, uncle, definitely! I'll never forget this year!
items: I tried, I've tried; have you tried? (to a man)
to a woman: jarrabti? (جربتي؟); I've tried it: jarrabtah
I rode, I went on (a camel, a boat)
I won't forget it (a feminine thing); with abad: I'll never forget it
a masculine thing: ma ansāh (ما أنساه)
we'll go out, we're heading out
I slept out in the desert, I camped in the desert
we slept out: nimna fi l-barr (نمنا في البر)
culture: in shāʼ allāh 'God willing' is the polite answer to an elder's invitation. It can be a real yes or a soft maybe, so if you mean yes, make it clear: in shāʼ allāh, akīd! or ask what time. If you can't come, thank him and give a reason.

title: What are you planning to do? nāwi
goal: At the office, tell Maryam your plans after the internship and ask about hers
tip: nāwi 'planning to' is a participle, so it agrees with whoever is planning: nāwi (a man), nāwya (a woman), nāwyīn (a group), then a present verb: nāwi akammil dirāsti. Asking a man: shu nāwi tsawwi?; a woman: shu nāwya tsawwīn? For the future, baʿd ma takes a present verb: baʿd ma titkharraj.
grammar: nāwi / nāwya + verb 'planning to'; recycle: future b-, baʿd ma
dialogue: A
شو ناوي تسوي بعد التدريب؟
shu nāwi tsawwi baʿd it-tadrīb?
What are you planning to do after the internship?
B
ناوي أكمل دراستي هني في دبي
nāwi akammil dirāsti hni fi Dbayy
I'm planning to carry on with my studies here in Dubai.
A
زين. وبعد ما تتخرج، شو خطتك؟
zēn. w baʿd ma titkharraj, shu khiṭṭatak?
Good. And after you graduate, what's your plan?
B
أبي أدور شغل هني
abi adawwir shughul hni
I want to look for a job here.
A
إن شاء الله! الله يوفقك
in shāʼ allāh! allāh ywaffgak
I hope so! Good luck.
B
آمين. وانتي، شو ناوية؟
āmīn. w inti, shu nāwya?
Amen. And you, what are you planning?
A
ناوية أخلص الماجستير، بس شو بعده؟ للحين ما قررت
nāwya akhalliṣ il-mājistēr, bas shu baʿdah? lil-ḥīn ma garrart
I'm planning to finish my master's, but what then? I haven't decided yet.
B
برأيي الماجستير أهم شي الحين. بتنجحين أكيد!
b-raʼyi l-mājistēr ahamm shay il-ḥīn. bitinjaḥīn akīd!
I'd say the master's is what matters now. You'll definitely do well!
items: planning to, intending to (a man); I'm planning to
what are you planning to do? (to a man)
to a woman: shu nāwya tsawwīn? (شو ناوية تسوين؟)
to a woman: baʿd ma titkharrajīn; after I graduate: baʿd ma atkharraj
what's your plan?: shu khiṭṭatak? (to a man), shu khiṭṭatich? (to a woman)
amen (the answer to a blessing such as allāh ywaffgak)
culture: Plans in the Gulf come wrapped in in shāʼ allāh. When someone tells you their plans, wish them well with allāh ywaffgak 'God grant you success' (to a woman: allāh ywaffgich). The answer is āmīn, and you can add a wish back: w inta baʿad 'and you too' (to a woman: w inti baʿad).

title: My dream since I was little
goal: At a karak stand one evening, hear Sēf's dream and tell him your ambition
tip: ḥilmi 'my dream' and ṭumūḥi 'my ambition' take inni 'that I' + a present verb: ḥilmi inni aṣīr ṭayyār 'my dream is to be a pilot'. aṣīr 'I become' also follows abi directly: abi aṣīr muhandis 'I want to be an engineer'.
grammar: ḥilmi, ṭumūḥi + present verb; recycle: abi + verb, lann
dialogue: A
تدري شو حلمي من صغري؟
tadri shu ḥilmi min ṣighri?
Do you know what my dream's been since I was little?
B
شو؟ تبي تصير لاعب كورة؟
shu? tabi tṣīr lāʿib kūra?
What? You want to be a footballer?
A
لا! حلمي إني أصير طيار، لأني أحب السفر
la! ḥilmi inni aṣīr ṭayyār, lanni aḥibb is-safar
No! My dream is to be a pilot, because I love travelling.
B
ما شاء الله! وللحين تبي تصير طيار؟
mā shāʼ allāh! w lil-ḥīn tabi tṣīr ṭayyār?
Wow! And do you still want to be a pilot?
A
أكيد! ما غيرت رأيي. وانت، شو حلمك؟
akīd! ma ghayyart raʼyi. w inta, shu ḥilmak?
Of course! I haven't changed my mind. And you, what's your dream?
B
طموحي إني أفتح شركة خاصة فيني. بس أول شي أبي أصير مهندس
ṭumūḥi inni aftaḥ sharika khāṣṣa fīni. bas awwal shay abi aṣīr muhandis
My ambition is to open my own company. But first I want to be an engineer.
A
إن شاء الله يتحقق حلمك. الله يوفقك!
in shāʼ allāh yitḥaggag ḥilmak. allāh ywaffgak!
I hope your dream comes true. Good luck!
B
آمين، وانت بعد!
āmīn, w inta baʿad!
Amen, and you too!
items: your dream: ḥilmak (to a man), ḥilmich (to a woman)
your ambition: ṭumūḥak (to a man), ṭumūḥich (to a woman)
I want to be, I want to become
you become: tṣīr (to a man), tṣīrīn (to a woman)
in shāʼ allāh yitḥaggag ḥilmak = I hope your dream comes true (to a man)

title: I feel Dubai's better for work: aḥiss inn
goal: Over coffee with Sēf and Fahad, say where you'd like to live after university and why
tip: aḥiss inn 'I feel (that)' gives an opinion from the heart: aḥiss inn Dbayy aḥsan lish-shughul. Before a pronoun, add the ending: aḥiss inni 'I feel I', aḥiss innah 'I feel he / it'. Ask lēsh tḥiss chī? 'why do you feel that way?' and answer with lann.
grammar: recycle: aḥiss + inn- 'I feel that'; opinions with lann
dialogue: A
بعد الجامعة، وين تبي تسكن؟ دبي ولّا لندن؟
baʿd il-jāmʿa, wēn tabi tiskin? Dbayy walla Landan?
After university, where do you want to live? Dubai or London?
B
صعب! بس أحس إن دبي أحسن للشغل
ṣaʿb! bas aḥiss inn Dbayy aḥsan lish-shughul
That's hard! But I feel Dubai's better for work.
A
ليش تحس جي؟
lēsh tḥiss chī?
Why do you feel that way?
B
لأن الفرص هني وايد، والناس طيبين
lann il-furaṣ hni wāyid, w in-nās ṭayybīn
Because there are lots of opportunities here, and the people are nice.
A
بس الغربة صعبة. ما تشتاق لأهلك؟
bas il-ghurba ṣaʿba. ma tishtāg l-ahlak?
But living away from home is hard. Don't you miss your family?
B
هيه، مشتاق لهم وايد. بس على الأقل لندن مب بعيدة
hē, mishtāg-lhum wāyid. bas ʿala l-aqall Landan mub baʿīda
Yes, I miss them a lot. But at least London isn't far.
A
وبصراحة، نحن ما بنخليك تروح!
w b-ṣarāḥa, niḥin ma binkhallīk trūḥ!
And honestly, we won't let you go!
B
عيل خلاص، أظن بقعد هني!
ʿayal khalāṣ, aẓunn bagʿid hni!
Well then, I think I'll stay here!
items: before a pronoun: aḥiss inni 'I feel I', aḥiss innah 'I feel he / it'
to a woman: tḥissīn (تحسين); why do you feel that way?: lēsh tḥiss chī?
living away from home, being abroad
to a woman: tishtāgīn (تشتاقين); don't you miss your family?: ma tishtāg l-ahlak?
I miss them (said by a man)
culture: il-ghurba is being far from your country and family, and the homesickness that comes with it. When Gulf friends ask a foreigner ma tishtāg l-ahlak? 'don't you miss your family?', it is a kind question. A warm answer about your family is the natural reply.

title: Checkpoint 3.5: where shall we have lunch?
goal: Checkpoint: the team project is nearly done; ask Maryam and the team where to have lunch afterwards, and wish them luck
tip: To a group, endings are -kum and -ūn: shu raʼykum? 'what do you all think?', tẓunnūn? 'do you all think?', bitiyūn? 'are you all coming?', allāh ywaffigkum 'good luck (all of you)'. To a woman: shu raʼyich?, tẓunnīn? A group participle takes -īn: nāwyīn 'we're planning'.
grammar: checkpoint 3.5: recycle s3u066–s3u082 (illi, aẓunn, b-raʼyi, nāwi, aḥiss)
dialogue: B
باقي لنا أسبوع على المشروع. شو رأيكم، وين نتغدى بعده؟
bāgi-lna usbūʿ ʿala l-mashrūʿ. shu raʼykum, wēn nitghadda baʿdah?
We've got a week left on the project. What do you all think, where shall we have lunch after it?
A
أظن المطعم اللي يم المترو. أكله زين
aẓunn il-maṭʿam illi yamm il-mitrō. aklah zēn
I think the restaurant by the metro. Its food's good.
B
مريم، شو رأيج؟ تظنين إنه زين؟
Maryam, shu raʼyich? tẓunnīn innah zēn?
Maryam, what do you think? Do you think it's good?
A
ما أظن، لأنه ما عاد مثل قبل
ma aẓunn, lannah ma ʿād mithil gabil
I don't think so, because it's not like it was before.
B
خلاص، اللي يبي ييي، ييي. والغدا علي، بتيون كلكم؟
khalāṣ, illi yabi yiyi, yiyi. w il-ghada ʿalay, bitiyūn killkum?
Right, whoever wants to come, comes. And lunch is on me: are you all coming?
A
أكيد! ونحن ناوين نخلص كل شي قبل الخميس
akīd! w niḥin nāwyīn nkhalliṣ kill shay gabil il-khamīs
Of course! And we're planning to finish everything before Thursday.
B
الله يوفقكم! وبرأيي المشروع اللي سويناه وايد زين
allāh ywaffigkum! w b-raʼyi l-mashrūʿ illi sawwēnāh wāyid zēn
Good luck! And in my opinion the project we've done is really good.
A
آمين، وانت بعد!
āmīn, w inta baʿad!
Amen, and you too!
items: what do you think? (to a woman)
to a man: shu raʼyak?; to a group: shu raʼykum?
to one man: tẓunn?; to one woman: tẓunnīn?
to a man: tẓunn?; to a group: tẓunnūn?
planning to, intending to (a group); we're planning to
one man: nāwi; one woman: nāwya
good luck, God grant you success (to a group)
to one man: allāh ywaffgak; to one woman: allāh ywaffgich; the answer: āmīn
will you come? are you coming? (to a group)
to one man: bitiyi?; to one woman: bitiyīn?
